definitions.explanation: The total set of questions on a test, quiz, or exam. Most commonly used in {全問|ぜんもん}{正解|せいかい} (all correct) and similar collocations.

examples.japanese: {全問|ぜんもん}{正解|せいかい}だった。
examples.english: I got all the questions right.

examples.japanese: {全問|ぜんもん}{解|と}くのに{一時間|いちじかん}かかった。
examples.english: It took me an hour to solve all the questions.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}のテストは{難|むずか}しくて、{全問|ぜんもん}{答|こた}えられた{生徒|せいと}は{一人|ひとり}もいなかった。
examples.english: This test was hard, and not a single student was able to answer every question.

notes:
Compound of {全|ぜん} (all) + {問|もん} (question/problem, used as a counter). Almost always used in school and test contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {全問|ぜんもん}{正解|せいかい}: all answers correct; perfect score
- {全問|ぜんもん}{不正解|ふせいかい}: all answers wrong
- {全問|ぜんもん}{解答|かいとう}: answering every question
- {全問|ぜんもん}{必答|ひっとう}: all questions must be answered

RELATED WORDS:
- {一問|いちもん}: one question
- {設問|せつもん}: a (test) question
- {満点|まんてん}: perfect score
